### 2026-10-31: October 30: #P0LAR15!!!

**4h**

October 30: #P0LAR15!!!

First day on working on it, I was surprised to see that the directions were quite vague and short, but I got over it, go check out READ.ME for most of my progress!!!

One mistake during this project was that I assigned the wrong footprints to C1, C2, R1, R2, the capacitors and resistors, they ended up being super huge!

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 211829](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UMx8GtS67VH17jO55ZdjXA5Q5GgA51Ts/7808de006a85a94407c759c2d7bce2b7d90adb860a2470f7a9aefcb589d76fa5.png)

Another mistake was that I put VCC for output 36 on the Pico, but since the OLED connector is +3V3, I had to switch VCC for +3V3:

![Screenshot 2026-10-27 161335](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UMx8GtS67VH17jO55ZdjXA5Q5GgA51Ts/04975696360b88a513404b04b7ed1c9c0f72a36a713f7f715949a3ca766a1ba0.png)

### 2026-11-01: Halloween: #P0LAR15!!!

**4h**

Halloween: #P0LAR15!!!

Happy Halloween ya'll and I got a great amount of progress today!

I rewired the PCB and changed some footprints on the schematic as I'm connecting my OLED to J2 (J1 is an alternative) and I believed for a temperature and humidity sensor, I didn't need the going further option:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UMx8GtS67VH17jO55ZdjXA5Q5GgA51Ts/6923fcea8833aaf45377f751e638d2d458c253da8c6be53e29a7722c4c64b21e.png)

Next was the Arduino coding, I installed the Adafruit GFX, the Adafruit SSD1306, and Raspberry Pi Pico/RP2040 by Earle F. Philhower. (this showed up by a custom link in the addit. URL's). Then I worked in the code and saved it to my folder shown here (make sure to define the code, or else the verification will go haywire):

### 2026-11-01: November 1: #P0LAR15!!!

**5h**

November 1: #P0LAR15!!!

Final day of the project, I got straight into work with following the Hermes guide, and after taking a look at it, I reallized that it was just adding the temperature and humidity sensor, it's footprints and PCB, and improving the code.

First, I had to choose which sensor I wanted, the DHT11 didn't match the I2C system, so I went for the SHT31 because the SHT30 was out of stock, AHT20 didn't work unlike the SHT31 because the PCBA type had to be economic.

Here is the sensor in the schematic, making sure the pins matched the order:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UMx8GtS67VH17jO55ZdjXA5Q5GgA51Ts/2c654e035163970ebdea9e939526c45d8bbbb08a71e93f3ff19d3cc660e52334.png)

Here is the assigned footprint, also forgot to mention this added another Capacitor, so there were some adjustments to the assigned footprints:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UMx8GtS67VH17jO55ZdjXA5Q5GgA51Ts/66acc241c927aad52f069a8352f1740e2e10adf68e5066b074580ac1bad6fc86.png)

Then comes the PCB editor, because there were 2 new components, I had to rewire EVERYTHING AGAIN:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UMx8GtS67VH17jO55ZdjXA5Q5GgA51Ts/5299f1fcb150d03b9f44a218e41af935b5f600632ec37824184fd2420d05b41c.png)

I also generated Gerber and Drill files, I had to replace my old ones on Kicad, and as always, I zipped the gerber and drill files and checked them on Gerber Viewer:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/UMx8GtS67VH17jO55ZdjXA5Q5GgA51Ts/936e8a37a9a378de85fc496033e30a9e53df2088ddb0c741b176519ca950a1d4.png)

After that, I improved the code with establishing the Sensor into the code and its functions:
